title: The Three-Qubit Bit-Flip Code
summary: The three-qubit bit-flip code, syndrome measurement and the threshold.
objectives: Encode a qubit into the three-qubit bit-flip code with two CNOT gates
Store the syndrome in two ancilla qubits without measuring the data qubits
Correct a single bit flip with Toffoli gates controlled by the syndrome
Predict that the code fails when two qubits flip
mission: Protect qubit 0 against bit flips. Encode it into three qubits (encode), store the syndrome in two ancillas without measuring the data qubits, and correct the flipped qubit (recover). The logical state must survive an X error on any one of the three qubits, for any input state.

prediction.question: An X error hits qubits 0 and 1 at the same time. What does the code do?
options: It fails: the syndrome points to qubit 2, and the result is a logical X
It destroys the state, which becomes a mixture
prediction.explanation: Flips on qubits 0 and 1 give the same syndrome as a single flip on qubit 2. The code applies X to qubit 2, so all three qubits end up flipped, which is a logical X. The code corrects one flip, not two.

hints: Encoding entangles the basis states instead of copying the state: qml.CNOT(wires=[0, 1]) and qml.CNOT(wires=[0, 2]) take α|0⟩ + β|1⟩ to α|000⟩ + β|111⟩.

Syndrome: ancilla 3 stores the parity of qubits 0 and 1 (CNOT from qubit 0 and from qubit 1 onto qubit 3), and ancilla 4 stores the parity of qubits 1 and 2. Each single flip gives a different pair of bits: X0 → 10, X1 → 11, X2 → 01.
Correction without measuring: qml.Toffoli(wires=[3, 4, target]) acts when both ancillas are 1. For a pattern with a 0, apply qml.PauliX to that ancilla before and after the Toffoli.
